articles.title: Most Americans don’t actually understand the judicial philosophies they endorse
articles.summary: A recent study in Political Research Quarterly suggests that while Americans claim to support specific judicial philosophies, most struggle to apply them consistently. For the general public, terms like originalism act more as symbolic labels than structured legal frameworks.

articles.summary: Miniature brain models grown from human stem cells show that different genetic forms of autism spectrum disorder produce vastly different patterns of electrical activity, revealing how various mutations alter neural networks.

articles.title: Semaglutide use is associated with a lower risk of adult-onset seizures
articles.summary: Adults with type 2 diabetes taking semaglutide might have a lower risk of developing seizures later in life. New research indicates this protective association is not entirely explained by weight loss, hinting at unique benefits for brain health.

articles.title: GeoID-PINN: Identifiability-Aware Regional Epidemic Inference with Geographic Coupling
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.02633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regional surveillance data reflect local transmission, reporting, seeding, and external infection pressure, which are difficult to identify separately. We introduce GeoID-PINN, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) for susceptible-infectious-recovered-deceased (SIRD) dynamics. The model represents spatial dependence with a row-stochastic source-composition matrix whose rows assign nonnegative source weights that sum to one. We regularize this matrix toward a spatial prior constructed from distance, adjacency, commuting, or lead-lag information

articles.title: Sitting up straight may improve your mood and decision-making
articles.summary: A simple change in posture may subtly affect how people feel and make decisions. Participants who sat upright reported greater feelings of pride and took more successful risks in a virtual balloon game than those who hunched over. Most did not realize researchers had influenced their posture, helping rule out the possibility that they were merely responding to expectations. The results suggest workplace ergonomics could influence more than physical comfort.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary: A group of brain cells called orexin neurons appears to help us keep working when reaching a reward becomes increasingly difficult. Blocking their activity weakened motivation in rats, pointing to a possible new target for understanding why people sometimes struggle to sustain goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: Study reveals a psychological link between feeling disadvantaged and using people
articles.summary: When people feel disadvantaged compared to their peers, they are more likely to view relationships as mere transactions. A new psychology study reveals how this sense of relative deprivation causes individuals to treat others as tools for personal gain.

articles.summary: New research published in Neurology suggests that adults over 80 who walk unusually fast experience slower mental decline. These "super movers" demonstrate powerful brain resilience, maintaining sharp minds despite typical markers of aging and disease.

articles.title: A simple 30-minute daily routine may help slow cognitive decline
articles.summary: A 12-week program requiring older adults to read out loud, write by hand, and solve basic math problems for 30 minutes a day resulted in measurable improvements on cognitive tests.

articles.title: New study details how ketamine alters neural networks differently in males and females
articles.summary: A recent study indicates that female mice experience distinct brain rewiring after ketamine anesthesia. Researchers found that a surge in the stress hormone corticosterone drives immune cells to build new neural connections, a process absent in males.

articles.title: Experts say blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
articles.summary: A new report suggests that blood pressure may be controlled more effectively by increasing potassium while also cutting sodium. Potassium-rich foods can help balance sodium’s effects, but most people consume far less potassium than recommended.

articles.title: Severe COVID-19 linked to anxiety in offspring via altered sperm RNA
articles.summary: A small study found that male mice infected with a severe form of SARS-CoV-2 passed anxiety-like behaviors to their offspring. The researchers traced these intergenerational changes to altered molecular messengers inside the fathers' sperm.
